# Release Notes - awake 0.3.0-beta

Release date: 2026-10-03 Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The third beta release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps the system awake. This release adds daemon autostart at logon, convenient command aliases and ships a fully modularized codebase.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project is generated by AI and has not been extensively reviewed. Please scrutinize the code carefully before use. The author is not responsible or liable for any consequences arising from the use of this software.

## Highlights

- **Daemon autostart at logon** (`awake daemon enable` / `disable`): optionally starts the daemon automatically when you log on. Written to the per-user registry Run key - no admin rights required. The current state is shown in `awake status`.
- **Command aliases** for quicker typing: `?`/`h` = help, `on`/`enable`/`start` = 1, `off`/`disable`/`stop` = 0, `st` = status, `scr` = screen, `screen 1/0` = `screen on/off`, `d` = daemon, `daemon 1/start` = `daemon on`, `daemon 0/stop` = `daemon off`.
- **Modularized codebase** (no functional change): the client and the daemon were split into small translation units, and the client/daemon wire protocol now lives in a single shared protocol module.

## Full command list

```
awake help              Show the help message (with version).
awake version           Show the version.
awake 0                 Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                 Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake status            Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                        watch list status.
awake screen on         Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                        and idle lock).
awake screen off        Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on         Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off        Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable     Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable    Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake reload            Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset             Reset the configuration file (asks for
                        confirmation).
awake add <imagename>   Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>   Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

See the command aliases note in `awake help` for the shorthand forms.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool. The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on first use.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only; after a daemon restart they are inactive again.
- The daemon sends a one-shot stay-awake notification when it starts, regardless of the current settings.
- If you enabled autostart and later move the executables to another folder, run `awake daemon enable` again in the new location.
- This is a beta release; the behavior and the command line interface may still change in incompatible ways before 1.0.
